metadata.title: AI Foundations Causal Inference — Sources
metadata.description: Primary academic references for 12 causal inference primitives: DAGs/SCMs, do-calculus, backdoor/frontdoor criteria, instrumental variables, RDD, DiD, synthetic control, propensity score methods, CATE/uplift, Simpson's paradox, mediation analysis, and sensitivity analysis.

foundational_books.name: Pearl — Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference (2nd ed.)
foundational_books.description: The canonical reference for DAGs, structural causal models, do-calculus, backdoor and frontdoor criteria, and counterfactual analysis. Chapters 1–3 cover the core identification theory underlying primitives #1–#3 and #10.

foundational_books.name: Imbens & Rubin — Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences
foundational_books.description: Canonical potential-outcomes framework reference. Covers IV, propensity scores, matching, and IPW. Primary source for primitives #4 and #8.

foundational_books.name: Angrist & Pischke — Mostly Harmless Econometrics
foundational_books.description: Applied econometrics bible for IV, RDD, and DiD. The standard reference for identification-assumption diagnostics in empirical work. Primary source for primitives #4, #5, #6.

foundational_books.name: Hernán & Robins — What If (freely available online)
foundational_books.description: Comprehensive causal inference textbook covering DAGs, time-varying treatments, IPW, and marginal structural models. Freely available. Primary source for primitives #1–#3 and #8.

foundational_books.name: VanderWeele — Explanation in Causal Inference: Methods for Mediation and Interaction
foundational_books.description: Canonical reference for causal mediation analysis using potential outcomes. Covers NDE, NIE, interaction, and sensitivity analysis for mediation. Primary source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: Pearl (1995) — Causal Diagrams for Empirical Research
research_papers.description: Original paper introducing the do-operator and do-calculus. Source for primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Imbens & Angrist (1994) — Identification and Estimation of LATE
research_papers.description: Foundational paper identifying the Local Average Treatment Effect via IV. Source for primitive #4.

research_papers.name: Imbens & Lemieux (2008) — Regression Discontinuity Designs: A Guide to Practice
research_papers.description: Practical guide to RDD: bandwidth selection, local linear regression, and validity tests. Source for primitive #5.

research_papers.name: Calonico, Cattaneo & Titiunik (2014) — Robust Nonparametric Confidence Intervals for RDD
research_papers.description: MSE-optimal bandwidth selection and bias-corrected CI for RDD. Source for primitive #5 bandwidth guidance.

research_papers.name: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) — Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods
research_papers.description: Staggered DiD estimator that avoids TWFE negative-weight bias under heterogeneous treatment effects. Source for primitive #6 staggered design guidance.

research_papers.name: Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2010) — Synthetic Control Methods
research_papers.description: Original synthetic control paper with the tobacco California case study. Source for primitive #7.

research_papers.name: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983) — The Central Role of the Propensity Score
research_papers.description: Original propensity score paper. Establishes balancing-score theorem and justification for propensity-based methods. Source for primitive #8.

research_papers.name: Chernozhukov et al. (2018) — Double/Debiased Machine Learning
research_papers.description: DML framework for Neyman-orthogonal, doubly robust treatment effect estimation using ML nuisance functions. Source for DR/R-learner in primitives #8 and #9.

research_papers.name: Colangelo & Lee (2025) — Double Debiased Machine Learning Nonparametric Inference with Continuous Treatments
research_papers.description: Extends DML to continuous treatment variables using kernel-based estimators for the average dose-response function (ADRF). Doubly robust to misspecification of one nuisance function; asymptotically normal with nonparametric convergence rates. Companion to Chernozhukov et al. (2018) for continuous treatment settings. Source for primitives #8 and #9 when treatment is continuous.

research_papers.name: Chernozhukov, Cinelli, Newey, Sharma & Syrgkanis (2026) — Long Story Short: Omitted Variable Bias in Causal Machine Learning
research_papers.description: General theory of omitted variable bias for DML/causal ML estimands (ATE, average causal derivatives, policy effects). Bounds bias using plausibility judgments on omitted-variable explanatory power; provides valid confidence intervals. Extends sensitivity analysis from OLS/IV to ML-estimated causal parameters. Implemented in the dml.sensemakr R package. Source for primitive #12 sensitivity in ML pipelines.

research_papers.name: Wager & Athey (2018) — Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
research_papers.description: Causal forests: asymptotically normal CATE estimation with honest sample splitting. Source for primitive #9.

research_papers.name: Athey & Imbens (2017) — The State of Applied Econometrics
research_papers.description: Survey of ML-based causal inference methods including CATE and meta-learners. Source for primitives #8 and #9.

research_papers.name: VanderWeele & Ding (2017) — Sensitivity Analysis in Observational Research: The E-Value
research_papers.description: Original E-value paper. Provides the formula and interpretive framework for sensitivity analysis of observational estimates. Source for primitive #12.

research_papers.name: Rosenbaum (2002) — Observational Studies (2nd ed.)
research_papers.description: The foundational reference for Rosenbaum bounds and sensitivity analysis in matched observational studies. Source for primitive #12.

research_papers.name: Cinelli & Hazlett (2020) — Making Sense of Sensitivity: Extending Omitted Variable Bias
research_papers.description: Partial R² approach to sensitivity analysis for regression-based estimates. Source for primitive #12 mean-difference sensitivity.

research_papers.name: Cinelli & Hazlett (2025) — An Omitted Variable Bias Framework for Sensitivity Analysis of Instrumental Variables
research_papers.description: Extends the partial-R² OVB sensitivity framework to IV estimates. Introduces IV robustness values quantifying the minimum confounder strength or exclusion-restriction violation needed to overturn conclusions. Implemented in the iv.sensemakr R package. Companion method to Cinelli & Hazlett (2020) for regression settings. Source for primitive #12 IV sensitivity.

research_papers.name: Borusyak, Jaravel & Spiess (2024) — Revisiting Event-Study Designs: Robust and Efficient Estimation
research_papers.description: Imputation estimator for staggered DiD: fit Y(0) model on never/not-yet-treated observations; impute counterfactuals for treated cells; take weighted average. Asymptotically efficient under unrestricted treatment-effect heterogeneity. Provides valid pre-trend tests and event-study plots. Requires no always-treated units. R/Stata packages: didimputation / did_imputation. Review of Economic Studies, Vol. 91, Issue 6, November 2024, pp. 3253–3285. doi:10.1093/restud/rhae011. Source for primitive #6 staggered DiD.

research_papers.name: Rambachan & Roth (2023) — A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends
research_papers.description: HonestDiD: sensitivity analysis for parallel-trends violations. Imposes restrictions on how much post-treatment trend violations can exceed pre-treatment violations; produces valid confidence intervals under those restrictions. Avoids the binary 'pass pre-trend test → proceed' logic. Review of Economic Studies, Vol. 90, Issue 5, October 2023, pp. 2555–2591. doi:10.1093/restud/rhad018. R/Stata package: HonestDiD. Source for primitive #6 parallel-trends robustness.

research_papers.name: Roth, Sant'Anna, Bilinski & Poe (2023) — What's Trending in Difference-in-Differences?
research_papers.description: Practitioner synthesis of the staggered-DiD revolution. Covers TWFE bias, heterogeneity-robust estimators (Callaway–Sant'Anna, Sun–Abraham, BJS, Gardner), parallel-trends relaxation (HonestDiD), and alternative inference frameworks. Journal of Econometrics, 235(2), 2218–2244, 2023. Canonical navigational reference for staggered-DiD method selection.

research_papers.name: Sun & Abraham (2021) — Estimating Dynamic Treatment Effects in Event Studies with Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
research_papers.description: Interaction-weighted estimator for staggered DiD. Decomposes TWFE coefficients by cohort to eliminate contamination across treatment-timing groups under heterogeneous treatment effects. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 175–199, 2021. Source for primitive #6 staggered DiD.

research_papers.name: Goodman-Bacon (2021) — Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment Timing
research_papers.description: Shows that the TWFE estimator equals a weighted average of all possible two-group/two-period DiD comparisons. Weights can be negative under heterogeneous treatment effects, explaining why TWFE is biased in staggered designs. The Goodman-Bacon decomposition is the diagnostic for identifying which comparison groups drive TWFE bias. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 254–277, 2021. Source for primitive #6 TWFE failure mode.

research_papers.name: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens & Wager (2021) — Synthetic Difference-in-Differences
research_papers.description: Synthetic DiD (SDiD): combines synthetic control unit weights with DiD time weights to jointly balance pre-treatment outcomes. Inherits robustness of synthetic control for few treated units while recovering DiD efficiency when units are many. American Economic Review, 111(12), 4088–4118, 2021. doi:10.1257/aer.20190159. R package: synthdid. Source for primitive #7 extension bridging SC and DiD.

research_papers.name: Sant'Anna & Zhao (2020) — Doubly Robust Difference-in-Differences Estimators
research_papers.description: Doubly robust DiD estimators that are consistent if either the propensity score or the outcome regression model is correctly specified. Provides the theoretical foundation for the doubly robust component of the Callaway–Sant'Anna (2021) estimator. Journal of Econometrics, 219(1), 101–122, 2020. Source for primitive #6 and #8 doubly robust estimation.

research_papers.name: Gardner (2022) — Two-Stage Differences in Differences
research_papers.description: Two-stage DiD: stage 1 regresses Y on unit and time fixed effects using untreated/not-yet-treated observations to estimate Y(0); stage 2 regresses residuals on treatment dummies. Robust to heterogeneous effects under staggered adoption; intuitive extension to event studies and covariates. R package: did2s. Working paper, arXiv:2207.05943, 2022. Source for primitive #6 staggered DiD.

research_papers.name: Baker, Callaway, Cunningham, Goodman-Bacon & Sant'Anna (2026) — Difference-in-Differences Designs: A Practitioner's Guide
research_papers.description: Current practitioner-facing synthesis of the DiD literature. Organizes DiD designs and estimators by target estimand, covariates, weights, multiple periods, and staggered timing rather than prescribing a single estimator; reiterates that TWFE misleads under heterogeneous effects and that pre-trend tests have limited power. Journal of Economic Literature, 64(2), 498–557, June 2026. Preprint: arXiv:2503.13323. Supersedes Roth et al. (2023) as the default navigational reference for primitive #6.

research_papers.name: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi & Zhao (2023) — Design and Analysis of Switchback Experiments
research_papers.description: Derives the optimal switchback design under assumptions on the order of the carryover effect, via a minimax discrete optimization formulation. The canonical reference for temporal-interference designs on a single shared system (pricing, matching, ranking). Management Science, 69(7), 3759–3777, 2023. Preprint: arXiv:2009.00148. Source for the Interference and SUTVA section in SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: Jia, Kallus & Yu (2025) — Clustered Switchback Designs for Experimentation Under Spatio-temporal Interference
research_papers.description: Handles spatial (graph-neighbor) and temporal (carryover) interference jointly by randomizing at the cluster-block level. Truncated Horvitz–Thompson estimator attains Õ(1/NT) MSE, matching the lower bound up to log terms for sparse graphs. Submitted December 2023; revised March 2025. Source for the combined spatio-temporal row of the interference design table in SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: Peng, Ye & Zheng (2025) — Differences-in-Neighbors for Network Interference in Experiments
research_papers.description: Differences-in-Neighbors (DN) estimator for network interference: bias is second-order in interference magnitude (vs first-order for difference-in-means) with variance exponentially smaller than Horvitz–Thompson. Composes with clustered designs for improved bias-variance tradeoffs. Validated on real social networks and ride-sharing simulations. Submitted March 4, 2025. Source for the graph-interference row of the interference design table in SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: Frauen et al. (2026) — Causal Methods for LLM Development and Evaluation
research_papers.description: Argues that central questions in LLM development and evaluation (data-mix effects, judge bias, prompt-to-model routing) are inherently causal and underserved by causal methods; logged LLM-pipeline data are subject to confounding and non-stationary deployment shift. Maps causal opportunities across the pipeline (pretraining, alignment, routing). Submitted May 25, 2026; published at KDD 2026. Source for the LLM Evaluation Pipeline composition recipe in SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: CausalBench (2024) — A Comprehensive Benchmark for Causal Learning Capability of Large Language Models
research_papers.description: Benchmark suite for LLM causal-learning capability across small (Asia, Cancer, Earthquake, Survey, Sachs) and medium (Child, Insurance, Alarm, Barley) bnlearn graphs. Notes that these standard graphs are widely published and plausibly present in pretraining corpora, so scores may reflect memorization rather than causal reasoning. Source for the benchmark-contamination caveat on LLM-assisted causal discovery in SKILL.md.

research_papers.name: LLM Cannot Discover Causality, and Should Be Restricted to Non-Decisional Support in Causal Discovery (2025)
research_papers.description: Argues LLM-proposed causal graphs should be treated as priors to seed DAG construction, not as identified causal models; edges must be validated with data-driven independence/faithfulness tests. Authors show LLM-guided heuristic search can still accelerate convergence in structure learning — the restriction is on decisional authority, not on all LLM use. Wu, Yu, Wu & Tan, submitted June 1, 2025. Source for the 'LLM-assisted causal discovery' note in SKILL.md.
